brief: Goldman's US equities desk frames November 5 as a violent risk-off day concentrated in semiconductors and AI-adjacent names (E&C, IPP/Power, Neoclouds), as the market re-prices datacenter GW build forecasts and capex execution risk following this week's election newsflow. SOX/semiconductor multiples have compressed roughly 50% from their June/July highs, and the desk sees the next investor debate as whether downside risk to GW/capex outlooks has now been overpriced. The tape: S&P -4.36% to 7,353 (worst since 4/4/25), NDX -6.36% to 26,629 (worst since March 2020), SOX -12%, High Beta Momentum -6.2% and now 51% off its June highs. VIX jumped to 27.77 and Nasdaq VIX had its biggest move since Covid; the desk's Vol Panic Index hit 9.3/10. Asset managers were net sellers of semis/AI with no offsetting hyperscaler/defensive-tech bid, unlike the prior day; hedge funds stayed roughly balanced while aggressively toggling shorts. Futures closed below the 7,549 CTA threshold, with the desk's morning estimate pointing to about $7.48bn of S&P supply for sale over the coming week.
